10.1002_adfm.77267: Pyrophosphate Na 3.12 Fe 2.44 (P 2 O 7 ) 2 (NFP) is noted for its stability and safety, yet kinetic and interfacial constraints limit performance. This work proposes a dopant‐free NFP cathode based on sodium (Na) deficiency chemistry. By precisely adjusting Na content, we synchronized local structure and charge compensation to develop a superior NFP‐3.05 cathode. Structural analysis reveals that moderate Na deficiency reduces oxygen vacancies and introduces Fe 3+ , thereby optimizing charge compensation while restoring Fe‐O‐P framework continuity. This enhances both Na + transport and electronic conductivity. Consequently, NFP‐3.05 delivers 104 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 C and maintains 91.2% capacity after 1500 cycles at 1 C, outperforming NFP‐3.12 and NFP‐2.98. In situ tests confirm high reversibility with a minimal 3.6% volume change. Notably, in situ DEMS reveals significantly suppressed gas evolution O 2 , CO 2 , CO/C 2 H 4 , proving that Na deficiency inhibits high‐voltage interfacial side reactions. To assess adaptability, we built additive‐free coin cells and additive‐based pouch cells. The coin cell achieved 92.2 mAh g −1 with 89.5% retention after 200 cycles at 1 C, verifying intrinsic compatibility. The pouch cell maintained 93.2% capacity after 150 cycles at 80 mA, demonstrating practical potential. This Na‐deficient strategy provides a pathway for optimizing NFP cathodes and a reference for synergistic structure‐interface regulation in polyanionic systems.
10.1021_acsami.6c02496: Developing efficient and durable anode electrocatalysts is essential for translating proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) into practical hydrogen production. Here, we report an Mn 2 O 3 supported RuO 2 electrocatalyst featuring short-range-ordered RuO 2 domains that synergistically combines high activity and durability for acidic oxygen evolution. Hydrothermal Ru deposition followed by calcination enables uniform RuO 2 dispersion on Mn 2 O 3, yielding edge-rich RuO 2 domains with limited long-range crystallinity. Structural characterization shows that RuO 2 /Mn 2 O 3 retained stable Ru speciation and an almost constant oxygen vacancy fraction after extended OER operation, consistent with suppressed anodic degradation. Operando spectroscopy captures the key *OOH and *OO intermediates, supporting an adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) under acidic conditions. Building on the identified AEM pathway and the stabilized catalyst structure, RuO 2 /Mn 2 O 3 achieves an overpotential of 150 mV at 10 mA cm –2, a Tafel slope of 44.6 mV dec –1, and stable operation for >400 h in acidic electrolyte. In PEMWE tests, RuO 2 /Mn 2 O 3 delivers 1.0 A cm –2 at 1.61 V and operates stably for 100 h at 200 mA cm –2, highlighting its promise for practical acidic water electrolysis.
10.1021_acsami.6c13634: Membrane-based gas separation technologies potentially offer energy-efficient and scalable solutions for various clean energy systems, carbon management, and industrial processing. As an alternative to conventional polymeric membranes that exhibit the traditional permeability-selectivity trade-off, mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) have emerged as a promising class that combines polymer processability with enhanced transport properties of porous materials, referred to as fillers. The fundamental design principles of MMMs are centered on tailoring transport properties to improve permeability-selectivity performance. However, in practice, MMM fabrication and optimization still rely heavily on simplified permeation predictions or modeling approaches that fail to capture the complex heterogeneous structures of these membranes. In this review, we aim to establish a continuum-scale framework for modeling gas permeation in MMMs by critically examining existing permeation models and presenting a unified description of transport mechanisms and their mathematical formulations. We highlight recent advances in transport modeling and discuss the role of microstructural representation in complementing these approaches, including advances in experimental imaging techniques and synthetic microstructure generation. We then identify key phenomena often simplified or overlooked in transport modeling development. Finally, we outline future perspectives for developing more predictive and physically grounded approaches to MMM design and material selection, while promoting a deeper mechanistic understanding of gas transport in complex MMM systems.
10.1021_jacs.6c21052: Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a practical route to fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.
10.1039_d6ta04485a: A scalable fabrication strategy produces hierarchical porous electrodes that regulate bubble evolution and gas–liquid transport, reducing concentration polarization and mass-transfer resistance for efficient industrial alkaline water electrolysis.
